h1:
Cafes in Sisaket Town
Good Coffee, Chill Vibes, Photo Corners
intro: Sisaket isn't just som tam and grilled chicken. Over the past few years a lot of cafes have popped up around town, from specialty spots roasting their own beans to clean, minimal white-toned rooms that photograph well. We've picked only places in town that are genuinely open and that locals drop by often, with the neighborhood, opening hours, drinks worth ordering, and rough prices for each.

blocks.html: Sisaket's town cafes cluster into just a few areas, mostly around Wan Luk Suea Road, Thepha Road, and the Mueang Tai–Mueang Nuea zones, all a few minutes' drive apart — so hopping between several in one day is easy. Most coffees run about 50–90 THB and pastries 50–120 THB a piece, which is reasonable compared with the bigger tourist towns. We've ordered the list by popularity and how often places come up in reviews, which doesn't mean the ones lower down are worse — each stands out in its own way. Some you go to for the coffee, others for the photo corners.

blocks.text: The Sisaket town cafes locals actually go to, ranked

blocks.html: All 10 of these sit inside Sisaket town or nearby, easy to reach. The prices listed are rough figures per cup or per piece and may shift with the menu and time of day. Opening and closing hours are taken from what each shop has announced — we'd suggest checking the shop's page again before you go, since some newer cafes change their hours often.

items.name: Caffeine Cafe & Roaster
items.blurb: A specialty cafe that roasts its own beans, sourced from several origins around the country. It's strong on pour-over and signature drinks like the Black Coconut and the Latte Dalgona, with fresh-baked pastries every morning. The shop is set in a small garden with both indoor and outdoor seating ringed by greenery, plenty of photo corners. If you're serious about coffee, start here.
items.meta: Soi Wichit Nakhon 13 (behind Mueang Sisaket Police Station) · open 07.30–18.30 daily

items.name: Cloud Cafe Sisaket
items.blurb: A minimal, white-toned cafe on Kasikam Road in the Mueang Tai area. Inside it's warm with several cute corners to photograph. The drink people talk about is the Umeshu Espresso Soda — coffee mixed with fizzy plum soda — good for anyone who likes a clean, quiet spot to sip.
items.meta: Kasikam Rd, Mueang Tai, Mueang district

items.name: Cafe De Tree
items.blurb: A vintage-style coffee shop on Thepha Road in the Mueang Nuea area, decked out with a mix of upscale and vintage touches and several photo corners. It's open long hours, from morning until late, so you can settle in all day. Recommended picks are the iced latte, coconut cake, and the red-syrup lime soda. You can eat well here for under 100 THB a head.
items.meta: 1291/5–6 Thepha Rd, Mueang Nuea, Mueang district · open 07.00–22.00 daily

items.name: Circles Coffee Roaster
items.blurb: A small roastery near Ruam Sai School, known for strong, dark coffee — try the Midnight Black — and fresh-baked croissants. The vibe is understated, leaning on coffee quality over flash. Good for people who like a dark roast and baked goods.
items.meta: Near Ruam Sai School, in town · open 08.00–17.30

items.name: Overlaugh Roaster
items.blurb: Another in-house roaster in town, near the Itim intersection. They roast their own coffee and serve coffee, matcha, and baked goods. The vibe is just right for working or settling in for a long chat, and locals who care about coffee come back often.
items.meta: Itim intersection area, in town · open 08.30–17.00

items.name: Vivid Cafe & Brunch
items.blurb: A cafe inside the Wichit Nakhon Hotel in the town center. The draw is having it all — coffee, brunch, one-plate meals, toast, and ice cream — which makes it good for a long, slow breakfast or late-morning meal. Handy if you're staying in town and want food and coffee in one place.
items.meta: Wichit Nakhon Hotel, town center · open 08.00–18.30

items.name: Fongnom Cafe & Bakery
items.blurb: A cafe on Wan Luk Suea Road with a simple feel, known for its iced green tea and mango bingsu, plus a bakery counter to choose from. Prices are easy on the wallet, good for an afternoon cool-down or grabbing pastries to go. It sits in the cafe cluster in the town center.
items.meta: Wan Luk Suea Rd, in town

items.name: ANDA Pâtisserie
items.blurb: A pastry-focused shop in town, strong on fresh-baked croissants and the chocolate-glazed Doyenne. The coffee is solid and plays well with the pastries. Good for anyone after quality baked goods at a reasonable price — grab some to go, or sit and pair a coffee with a pastry.

items.name: TAEMICK Cafe & Garden
items.blurb: A garden-style cafe in town that's open most of the day, with coffee, dim sum, breakfast, rice porridge, and baked goods. Good for coming as a group or family — easy seating, an airy feel with plenty of greenery, and fine for kids too.

items.name: Napapa.house
items.blurb: A warm, homey cafe across from the waterworks, known for its carrot cake and Thai tea, with solid coffee. The atmosphere is quiet and calm, good for going solo or chatting one-on-one. Prices are easy on the wallet, and it's a place the neighborhood regulars keep coming back to.
items.meta: Across from the waterworks, in town · open 09.00–17.00

blocks.title: Straight talk on opening hours
blocks.html: A lot of Sisaket cafes are newer spots, and their hours and weekly closing days change often — some close on Mondays or take days off without much warning. Before you drive over, check the shop's Facebook page or Instagram day by day so you don't waste the trip, especially if you're set on just one place.

blocks.text: Pick a cafe by the style you're after

blocks.html: If you'd rather not hop between several places, it's easier to choose by what you want. Coffee people should stick to the in-house roasters, photo people to the good-looking rooms, and groups or families to a place that also serves food so you can linger longer.

items.name: Specialty coffee crowd
items.blurb: Caffeine, Circles, and Overlaugh roast their own beans, with pour-over and signature drinks that focus on the actual taste of the coffee.

items.name: Photo crowd
items.blurb: Cloud Cafe in clean minimal white and Cafe De Tree in vintage style, both with plenty of corners that photograph well.

items.name: Groups & families
items.blurb: Vivid and TAEMICK serve one-plate meals and brunch, fine for lingering and good for kids.

items: Wan Luk Suea Road–Soon Heng intersection — the central cafe zone, with several shops within walking distance, including Fongnom and the Caffeine branch by the Soon Heng intersection.
Thepha Road, Mueang Nuea area — Cafe De Tree and the vintage spots are around here, good for settling in over the evening.
Mueang Tai zone (Kasikam Rd) — Cloud Cafe and the minimal white-toned spots, focused on photos.
Around the town center — hotel cafes like Vivid and small roasters are scattered about, all a few minutes' drive apart.

blocks.title: If you're heading on toward the border
blocks.html: If you plan to do town cafes and then drive on to Pha Mo I Daeng or Khao Phra Wihan National Park in the south of the province, always check the border situation and whether the area is open before you set out — some periods it may be closed or restricted. Keep a backup plan ready too.

blocks.text: Doing Sisaket cafes right, the local way

items: At in-house roasters like Caffeine and Circles, order a pour-over or a black coffee to really taste the beans.
Popular cafes get busy on weekends — if you want good photo corners, go right at opening in the morning when it's emptier.
Many shops take PromptPay, but carry some cash too in case a smaller place's system goes down.
If you want to work, pick an indoor spot with outlets like Overlaugh or Vivid for convenience.
Driving between shops is easy and parking is simple to find, but the town center gets busy in the evening, so allow extra time.

faq.q: Which Sisaket town cafe has genuinely good coffee?
faq.a: For specialty coffee, go with Caffeine Cafe & Roaster, which roasts its own beans and is strong on pour-over. Next are Circles Coffee Roaster for its dark coffee and Overlaugh Roaster, another in-house roaster in town. All three focus on bean quality over flash.

faq.q: Where are the photo-friendly cafes in Sisaket?
faq.a: Cloud Cafe in the Mueang Tai area is clean, minimal and white-toned for nice photos. Cafe De Tree on Thepha Road has vintage decor with plenty of corners, and Caffeine has an outdoor garden zone with several photo spots too. Pick whichever style you like.

faq.q: How much do coffee and pastries cost at Sisaket cafes?
faq.a: Most coffees run about 50–90 THB a cup, with pastries and cakes around 50–120 THB a piece and bingsu about 90–150 THB. It's reasonable — at many places you can sit all day for under 200 THB a person.

faq.q: Are the cafes in Sisaket close together — can you do several in one trip?
faq.a: Yes. The town cafes cluster around Wan Luk Suea Road, Thepha Road, and the Mueang Tai–Mueang Nuea zones, all a few minutes' drive apart with easy parking, so doing two or three in one day is no problem. Just check each shop's hours before you go.

faq.q: Do any Sisaket cafes open late or early?
faq.a: Both. Coffee-focused spots like Caffeine open from 07.30, good for breakfast, while Cafe De Tree and TAEMICK stay open past 10 p.m., good for the evening. Hours change often, though, so check the shop's page before you go.
